examples.purpose: Comparing gold coins, the guide's In context: people add coins from the Gold coins list, and the bar fills from the left. Here the 1 g coin is added, so its picture fills the first slot (named for screen readers) and Compare is on. Tapping its picture takes the coin out (onItemRemove), an empty slot asks the screen to add the next coin (onItemPress), and the screen opens the comparison (onCompare). The rows leave out the guide's leading pictures, and their Buttons carry no modes.

props.name: items
props.description: The bar keeps no state: your screen updates items. Declared: The slots rendered before the Compare button. Each entry controls its own add/image state via {@link ComparisonBarItem.imageSource}.

props.name: onItemPress
props.description: Fired when an empty (Add) slot is tapped. The consumer is expected to react by opening whatever picker is appropriate and then updating that item's `imageSource` to flip it into the "Image Added" state — the component does not know how images are sourced. Receives the item's `id` (or index when no id was supplied) and the slot index.

props.name: onItemRemove
props.description: Fired when a filled slot is tapped. For better mobile ergonomics the *entire* filled slot is the remove target (the dismiss capsule is just a visual affordance), so a fingertip anywhere on the item triggers this. The consumer is expected to clear that item's `imageSource` to return it to the "Add" state. Receives the item's `id` (or index) and the slot index.

props.name: onCompare
props.description: Fired when the Compare button is pressed.

props.name: compareLabel
props.description: Label for the trailing action button. Defaults to `"Compare"`. Default "Compare", from the component source.

props.name: compareDisabled
props.description: Set to true or false, it overrides the automatic behaviour both ways. Declared: Explicitly controls the Compare button's *functional* disabled state — a truly disabled button is non-interactive (its `onPress` never fires), not just dimmed. Note that `modes` only affects appearance, so dimming the button via tokens does NOT stop taps; that is what this prop is for. When provided (a boolean), it always wins over {@link ComparisonBarProps.disableCompareWhenEmpty}. Leave it `undefined` to fall back to the auto behavior.

props.name: disableCompareWhenEmpty
props.description: While no slot has an image, Compare is off: 50 % opacity and not pressable. One image turns it on. Declared: When `true` (default) the Compare button is automatically (and truly) disabled while no slot has an image — there is nothing to compare yet. Set to `false` to keep it tappable even when empty. Ignored when {@link ComparisonBarProps.compareDisabled} is set explicitly. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: modes
props.description: Mode configuration passed to the token resolver.

props.name: style
props.description: Style overrides for the outer floating card.

props.name: ComparisonBarItem.id
props.description: Stable identifier for this slot. Returned to callbacks so the consumer can target the exact item that was interacted with. Falls back to the array index when omitted. A field of each items row.

props.name: ComparisonBarItem.imageSource
props.description: Set, the slot is filled: its picture and a close mark. null, undefined or an empty string leave it empty, with a +. Declared: Image to render in the slot. When provided the slot renders in the "Image Added" state; when omitted/`null` it renders the empty "Add" state. Accepts the same shapes as the library `Image` component (remote URL string, `{ uri }`, or a `require()`d asset). A field of each items row.

props.name: ComparisonBarItem.accessibilityLabel
props.description: Names the slot. Left out, an empty slot is “Add item to comparison” and a filled one “Remove item from comparison”. Declared: Accessibility label for the slot. Defaults to a generic add/remove label. A field of each items row.

modes.name: AppearanceBrand
modes.description: Brand modes on the bar also reach the empty slots' +: on Secondary, Neutral or Tertiary (or Semantic Intent System) it turns white, about 1.19:1 on the slot, and on Emphasis Medium faint gold. Declared: A token collection ComparisonBar reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

gaps.text: Brand modes on the bar turn the empty slots' + white (Component Bug #421).
Figma's Compare button is 96 × 32 and pale purple (the values of Button Size S, Secondary, Disabled); the package draws a size M gold Button, dimmed by opacity when off (Component Bug #421).
The empty slot's + is 18 px (XS) where Figma's is 29 px with an 18 px glyph (S), though the package's own comment says S (Component Bug #421).
A filled slot's picture is 33 × 28 where Figma's is 33 × 20, and the bar's right padding is 12 px where Figma's is 8 (Component Bug #421).
The slots give no press feedback (Component Bug #421).
The bar has no overflow handling (Component Bug #421).
Figma's Code Connect passes a Button child; the package takes items and compareLabel.
Biscuit's ComparisonBar.mdx mentions “the disabled-style props”; the props are compareDisabled and disableCompareWhenEmpty.
